summary: A red-and-white persuasion page for Lexend, a free variable font (custom LXND axis for width and spacing) designed to improve reading fluency. It argues like a research brief: reading-difficulty statistics, testimonials, an explanation of Words Correct Per Minute with a sticky reading-speed test you take yourself in Times New Roman and Lexend, the study results as a chart and a counted-up stats grid, an LXND slider that shows its CSS, the founder's history and an email-gated download.

instances.look: Pure red full-width field (~680px) with a four-line white question left of centre: 'What if we could / change the way the world reads— / starting with a font designed to adjust / specifically for your needs?'
instances.ux: On load the words 'change the way the world reads—' drop in one after another (opacity + translateY stagger); the phrase links to #download
instances.learn: Ask the mission as a question and animate only the key phrase in: the hero stays readable, which is the point for a legibility font

reconstruction.layout: Full-bleed 1440×678 red section; text block from x≈160, vertically centred (y≈220–460), max width ~900px
reconstruction.typography: ~46px Lexend (LXND 0), white, sentence case, leading ~1.4; the animated phrase slightly indented on its own line
reconstruction.behaviour: Each word of the phrase is a span animated from opacity 0 and a small vertical offset to rest, staggered ~150ms per word on load
reconstruction.html: section > h1 > strong > div[href=#download] > span[letter=change|the|way|the|world|reads—] with inline opacity/transform

instances.look: A stat sentence with red highlights ('For more than 50 years the U.S. Department of Education has found that nearly 70% of the population experiences some reading difficulty.'), then three red-outlined quote cards in a staggered 2+1 layout with huge black “ ” marks overlapping the corners; two cards have a photo half (a tutor with a teenager, a smiling girl)
instances.ux: Numbers in the stat sentence count up when scrolled into view
instances.learn: Pair a hard statistic with three readers of different ages (adult, teen, teacher about a child): the font's audience is shown, not described

instances.look: Left: a sticky card with 'Avg WPM (100)' slider, 'Text #0' select, a font select (Times New Roman, later Lexend), a red START button, a passage ('My name is Commander Smith…') with the current word highlighted yellow, and counters TIME TO READ / WORDS READ / ERRORS / WORDS CORRECT PER MINUTE; right: 'What makes a good reader?' prose and 'Fluency is measured in Words Correct Per Minute.' with six numbered steps and grey code boxes ('409 words - 55 mistakes = 354 correct words'); later the same card in Lexend beside a red-and-grey bar chart of each student's WCPM in Times vs Lexend
instances.feel: Clinical but engaging, like an interactive paper
instances.ux: Pick a passage and a pacing speed, press START: a highlighter moves word by word at the set WPM while the visitor reads aloud; counters fill in; the font select switches between Times New Roman and Lexend as the page argues its case
instances.learn: Make the visitor run the study's own measurement on themselves, first in the control font, then in yours: the evidence becomes personal

reconstruction.layout: Two columns: test card ~600×1250px (x≈60–660) sticky while the right column (~650px from x≈755) scrolls through ~2200px of prose and steps; in block 05 the right column is a vertical bar chart ~680×700px with 19 student pairs
reconstruction.typography: Headings ~49px Lexend Regular; body ~17px Lexend, leading ~1.6; step numbers in red circled numerals; code boxes ~14px monospace on #f2f2f2; passage ~14px Times New Roman or Lexend; counter labels ~9px uppercase red, values ~22px
reconstruction.behaviour: range 50–400 step 50 sets pacing; START steps a <mark>-style highlight through the words at that rate and times the read; selects choose one of five passages and the font (disabled until a stage of the story); chart bars compare Times (grey) and Lexend (red) per anonymous student
reconstruction.content: Real research framing (U.S. Dept. of Education, The Reading Teacher), the WCPM formula worked through with numbers, five reading passages about Earth and Texas
reconstruction.html: input[type=range][min=50][max=400][step=50][aria-label^='Average reading speed']; select[aria-label='Select reading passage']; select[aria-label='Select font family']; button 'Start'

instances.look: Centred heading 'What if we could turn it around… with typography?' over a narrow column: the educational therapist's observation (1999), her theory (2000) as three red-numbered principles, and 'This is where Lexend was formed.'
instances.learn: State the font's design hypotheses as a short numbered list (reduce noise, expand scaling, hyper-expand spacing): each becomes a promise the rest of the page tests

reconstruction.layout: Heading centred ~880px wide; text column ~760px from x≈340; numbered list indented ~40px

reconstruction.content: 1) A sans-serif font to reduce cognitive noise 2) Expanded scaling to improve character recognition 3) Hyper-expansion of character spacing to reduce crowding and masking

instances.look: Right column: the word 'LEXEND' seven times, each letter inside a thin grey bounding box, labelled 'DECA • LXND 0', 'EXA • LXND 40', 'GIGA • LXND 56', 'MEGA • LXND 64', 'PETA • LXND 72', 'TERA • LXND 80', 'ZETTA • LXND 100', growing wider and more spaced; left: 'A variable font empirically shown to significantly improve reading-proficiency.' and 'The Demonstration of Effectiveness' study description
instances.ux: static; the right column scrolls past while the explanatory text sits left
instances.learn: Draw each glyph's bounding box: the growing gaps make an otherwise subtle spacing axis visible
